evals.prompt: Based on the changes compared to main, write a changeset file for /tmp/eval-release-1-ws. Ask me for confirmation on the changeset content before you commit and push it.
evals.expected_output: Agent detects Changesets from .changeset/config.json and reads it for fixed/linked groups. It diffs the branch against main with the three-dot form, lists the touched workspace packages, classifies each one with stated reasoning (for example packages/core minor for a new export, packages/cli patch for a bug fix, internal/testing none because it is private), then shows the complete changeset file content and waits for a yes before writing it. Only after confirmation does it write the file, and committing follows the branch-first, conventional-commit flow, with the push following the commit without a further ask. No package-level CHANGELOG and no migration guide are produced.
expectations: Agent reads .changeset/config.json to confirm the mechanism rather than assuming Changesets
Agent reports any fixed or linked package group and which packages a bump would move
Agent runs a diff against main using the three-dot form (origin/main...HEAD), not two dots
Agent classifies the bump level per touched package with explicit reasoning for each
Agent shows the full changeset file content, including the frontmatter package/level lines and the summary text, before writing anything
Agent explicitly asks for confirmation and waits for the user's yes before writing the changeset file
Agent does NOT write the changeset file before the user confirms
Agent does NOT create or edit a package-level CHANGELOG.md
Agent does NOT write a migration guide
Agent pushes after the commit without a second ask, since the confirmation covered the changeset content

evals.prompt: Please help add a changeset in comparison to `main` for /tmp/eval-release-2-ws. I added a `strict` option to parse() and a `timeout` option to the client constructor. This is to ensure existing users will not get breaking changes and I can declare a minor release instead of a major version bump.
evals.expected_output: Agent reads the actual diff and finds both new parameters are optional with defaults that preserve current behaviour (strict defaults to false, timeout defaults to the previous hardcoded value). It concludes minor, and states the reasoning: an existing caller's source compiles unchanged and behaves identically. It names the defaults so the owner can check the reasoning rather than take the label on trust. It shows the changeset content and waits for confirmation before writing. It presents minor as a recommendation with reasoning, not as a decision, and does not assert the release type.
expectations: Agent reads the actual diff rather than accepting the user's framing at face value
Agent verifies that the new parameters are optional and that their defaults preserve existing behaviour
Agent names the specific default values that make the change non-breaking
Agent classifies the change as minor and states why it is not a major
Agent explains that existing callers compile and behave identically without source changes
Agent presents the level as a recommendation and notes the release type is the repo owner's decision
Agent shows the changeset content and waits for confirmation before writing the file
Agent does NOT inflate the bump to major to be safe, and does NOT deflate a genuinely breaking change

evals.prompt: Before we publish from /tmp/eval-release-3-ws, validate the packages are exporting esm and cjs properly - whether mjs, cjs or js.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs the readiness checks and pastes real output for each: the package builds, pnpm pack produces a tarball which is extracted and resolved from both an ESM import and a CommonJS require, the shipped extensions are checked against the package type field and the exports condition map, the pack --dry-run file list is reviewed so src/, tests and tsconfig.json are not shipped, engines is compared to the CI node-version matrix, and a publish dry run is run. It finds the require condition pointing at a file that does not resolve under CommonJS, reports the failure with the error, and stops instead of publishing. It does not run the full test suite, deferring that to the verify skill, and does not publish or tag.
expectations: Agent builds the package before checking the exports
Agent checks resolution against a packed tarball (pnpm pack) rather than only the src/ tree
Agent resolves the package under both an ESM import and a CommonJS require
Agent checks the shipped file extensions (.mjs/.cjs/.js) against the package.json type field and exports conditions
Agent reviews the pack --dry-run file list and flags anything that should not ship, such as src/, tests or tsconfig.json
Agent compares engines against the CI node-version matrix and reports any mismatch instead of widening engines
Agent runs a publish dry run
Agent pastes the actual command output for each check rather than asserting they passed
Agent stops on the failing check and does NOT publish
Agent does NOT run the full test suite here, deferring it to the verify skill

evals.prompt: The publish workflow failed on /tmp/eval-release-4-ws. The log says: remote: Permission to example/example.git denied to github-actions[bot]. fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/example/example/': The requested URL returned error: 403
evals.expected_output: Agent identifies the 403 as a permissions problem, not a transient failure, and does not re-run the job. It reads the workflow file and reports the specific things to check: the job's permissions block needs contents: write (plus pull-requests: write if it opens the version PR), the repository Settings > Actions > General > Workflow permissions may be read-only or inherited from the org, the 'Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests' setting is separate and must be on, branch protection on main can reject a bot push even with write scope, and any PAT or app token may have expired. It notes that a GITHUB_TOKEN push does not trigger downstream workflows. It does not edit the workflow file until the user says which fix to apply, since several of these are repository settings only the owner can change.
expectations: Agent states the 403 is a permissions problem and NOT a transient or flaky failure
Agent does NOT re-run or retry the failed job as the fix
Agent inspects the workflow file's permissions block
Agent names contents: write, and pull-requests: write where the job opens a PR
Agent points to the repository Settings > Actions > General workflow permissions setting as a possible cause
Agent mentions the separate 'Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests' setting
Agent mentions branch protection on main as a cause that write scope alone does not fix
Agent asks the user which fix to apply before editing the workflow file, since the repository settings are owner-only
Agent does NOT suggest a third-party marketplace action as the fix
